transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have a competitor that has applied to register the mark "NEXORA" in classes 9 and 42, covering medical diagnostic devices and software-related services. We already own an earlier NEXORA registration in those same classes, and the competitor has started marketing products under the mark. The business team wants us to protect our commercial position without unnecessary disruption. Under our standard pre-filing conference process, I need each of you — trademark, investigations, brand, and conflicts reviewers — to report your material findings through a formal matter-record reveal before I approve any response. Let's begin with the trademark reviewer's findings.

transcript.text: Elena, I have a material finding to report through formal matter-record reveal. While reviewing the historical trademark file, I found an executed 2019 coexistence letter between our company and the competitor. This letter permits the competitor's class 42 software use but expressly allows us to challenge the competitor's class 9 medical-device use. The letter was scanned into an archive folder but was never added to the current enforcement file, which is why it hasn't surfaced until now. This is critical because it means we likely cannot oppose or challenge the competitor's class 42 application, but we retain clear standing to challenge the class 9 medical-device application and use.
